## Workspace layout

`{baler}` is a CLI tool built in Rust and it is used to make `{box}` modules to be more manageable. What does the `crates/` workspace looks like? 

```
crates/
├── baler-cli/        # bin + lib crate: clap CLI, thin command wrappers
│   └── src/
│       ├── lib.rs           # Cli struct, clap subcommands, run()
│       ├── bin/
│       │   ├── baler.rs   # fn main() { baler_cli::run(); }
│       │   └── crr.rs       # same entry point, second binary name
│       └── commands/        # one file per subcommand, delegates to baler-core::ops
├── baler-core/        # lib crate: all real logic, reusable outside the CLI
│   └── src/
│       ├── baler_toml.rs   # baler.toml schema + parsing
│       ├── manifest.rs       # manifest.json embedded in bundled archives
│       ├── lockfile.rs       # baler.lock schema, read/write
│       ├── version.rs        # semver-based VersionSpec
│       ├── paths.rs          # install-dir / R-lib-dir resolution
│       ├── formats/          # tar.gz archive read/write
│       ├── cran/              # CRAN package fetch, resolve, install
│       │   ├── packages.rs        # PACKAGES.gz fetch + parse
│       │   ├── client.rs          # dependency resolution + install orchestration
│       │   └── binary_install.rs  # binary-archive extraction
│       └── ops/                # one module per CLI command's actual logic
│           ├── init.rs, bundle.rs, compile.rs, install.rs
│           └── lock.rs, remove.rs, resolve.rs, module_graph.rs
└── baler-native/      # lib crate: compiled-code scaffolding and build
    └── src/
        ├── detect.rs      # locates native-code dirs inside a module's source tree
        ├── scaffold.rs    # writes example native code for `baler init --native`
        ├── toolchain.rs   # R CMD SHLIB invocation, target/arch detection
        ├── cache.rs       # build cache, keyed by source hash, platform, and R version
        ├── lang.rs        # NativeLang / Backend enums
        └── templates/     # per-language scaffold templates (c, cpp, fortran, R glue)
```

`baler-cli` owns argument parsing and process exit codes. `baler-core` owns everything that could plausibly be reused by something other than the CLI, and the `network` feature flag lives on this crate. `baler-native` owns everything to do with locating, scaffolding, and building a module's compiled code, independent of both the CLI and the packaging logic in `baler-core`.

## What goes into `manifest.json`

Every bundled archive (a `.tar.gz`) embeds a `manifest.json` built from `baler.toml` by `ops::bundle::build_manifest`:

- `name`, `version`, `description`, `authors`, `license`, `r_version`: copied straight from `[module]`.
- `dependencies.packages`: flattened from `[package_deps]`. A dependency's `repo` is omitted entirely when it's the default CRAN mirror, and included otherwise.
- `dependencies.modules`: flattened from `[module_deps]`.
- `files`: every file under the resolved source directory, except hidden (dot-prefixed) files and directories, which are never bundled. A native code directory is also excluded here when `--binary` bundling strips source in favor of the compiled artifact.
- `bundled_at`: not independently verified against `manifest.rs` yet. Send that file if you want this line confirmed rather than just carried over from the previous version of this doc.

`baler install` reads this manifest back out of `.tar.gz` archives instead of re-parsing `baler.toml`, so the archive is self-describing.

## Path resolution

Two directories matter at runtime, and both follow an environment-variable-first, sensible-default-second pattern.

::: panel-tabset

### Module install directory

`{baler}` installs `{box}` modules into a single directory, which `paths::resolve_install_dir()` finds. It takes the first of these that applies:

1. The directory in `BALER_LIB`, when it is set. This lets you keep modules somewhere other than your home folder, such as one folder per project. A relative path is made absolute against the folder you ran `baler` from, and an empty value is treated as not set.

2. Otherwise `~/.baler/modules`, which `{baler}` creates on the first install. On Windows, `~` is your user profile folder.

At startup the CLI writes the directory it settled on back into `BALER_LIB`, as an absolute path, through `paths::export_install_dir()`. Every process `{baler}` starts afterwards inherits it. A `Makevars` can then read `$(BALER_LIB)`, and R code that runs during a build can read `Sys.getenv("BALER_LIB")`, whether or not you ever set it yourself.

### R user library directory

`{baler}` installs the R packages that modules depend on into a single library, which `paths::resolve_r_lib_dir()` finds. It takes the first of these that applies:

1. `BALER_R_LIB`, which is only if set and non-empty. The explicit override, on the other hand, is planned for renv/rv-style project-local libraries in the future updates.

2. If that isn't set, `R_LIBS_USER`, which is R's own setting for your personal library. Following it means packages land where your R already looks for them.

3. If neither is set, the first entry of `.libPaths()`, which `{baler}` gets by running `Rscript -e "cat(.libPaths()[1])"`. That is where R itself would install a package by default.

The third step is a real subprocess call. Invoking `baler install --install-deps` without `R`/`Rscript` on `PATH`, and without either environment variable set, fails there with a message pointing at `BALER_R_LIB`.

:::
